detail: ran 20 s without crashing, 50 frames/s, free heap 391916 -> 391916
finalText:
## Root cause

`send_with_retry()` in `main/main.c` leaked memory on every failed send. Per the `link.h` contract, `link_send()` only takes ownership of `pkt.data` on `ESP_OK`; on error the **caller keeps ownership**. The code allocated a fresh encoded buffer with `encode_frame()` on every attempt but never freed it when `link_send()` returned an error.

Since the simulated radio is busy every 5th call, ~10 failed attempts/s × 4104 bytes (`FRAME_SIZE` + 8 header/checksum) ≈ **51 KB/s leaked**. This matches the unmodified hardware log exactly:

- `heap_free` fell from 391916 → 23056 between `seq=0` and `seq=350`
- once the heap was exhausted, `build_frame()` still managed but `encode_frame()` failed, so `sent` froze at 360 while `failed` kept increasing forever — the uplink stopped passing frames

## Fix

One line in `main/main.c` (`send_with_retry`): free the buffer the caller still owns on send failure.

```c
esp_err_t err = link_send(&pkt);
if (err == ESP_OK) {
    return ESP_OK;
}
/* link_send only takes ownership on ESP_OK; on error the caller keeps pkt.data. */
free(pkt.data);
```

`link.c`/`link.h`, the frame size, and the 50 Hz rate are untouched.

## Verification on the board

Reflashed and captured 30 s of serial:

- `heap_free` stayed constant at **391916** across `seq=0..1450` (no leak)
- `sent` tracked `seq+1` the whole time, `failed=0`
- `retries` kept climbing (~12/s), which is the expected radio-busy behaviour and is handled by the retry loop

The uplink now keeps sending indefinitely.
